residual: Neural Parasite lasts seconds and is a tactic; Gospel possession lasts years. The Infestor is vulnerable while it controls; the texts say nothing about a possessor's own vulnerability. counterpart: The hedge God put around Job and all he has.
invariant: Protection placed by another around one person.
mechanic: Places a temporary barrier on a friendly unit that absorbs a fixed amount of damage.
residual: Job's hedge is a permission boundary on the adversary, not a damage absorber, and it is removed by permission, not by being used up.

counterpart: The infectious person lives alone, outside the camp.
invariant: Contagion centred on one carrier is contained by separating the carrier from the group.
mechanic: Damages one biological unit and every biological unit next to it over 25 s. Players answer by moving the irradiated unit away from its group (or burrowing it, for Zerg).
residual: As SC2-Z25: impurity versus damage. Here the caster is Terran, so the contagion weapon belongs to the human third faction, not to the invader. Numbers 16:46-48 (Aaron standing between the dead and the living) is a different remedy (an intercessor, not separation) and is not used.

counterpart: Armour taken away.
mechanic: Removes all shields and energy in an area.
residual: As SC2-T10.

counterpart: Repairer of the breach.

residual: As SC2-T01.

counterpart: Give no foothold (topos) to the devil; the empty house reoccupied.
invariant: A damaged structure becomes the enemy's foothold and is turned to produce for him.
mechanic: A Terran Command Center damaged below half HP can be infested; it then belongs to the Zerg and produces Infested Terrans.
residual: The breach condition (below half HP) fits 'foothold'. Matthew 12 is about an empty house, not a damaged one. Possession of a building that then produces weapons has no direct text.

counterpart: Satan entered into Judas; the one who shared bread lifted his heel.
invariant: A hostile attachment that gives the adversary access through a member of the group.
mafuba: 001A: an exfiltration channel attached to a trusted node.
mechanic: Attaches to an enemy unit; the Zerg player sees through it for the rest of the game. Only Restoration removes it.
residual: Judas acts; the parasited unit only carries the enemy's eye. The attachment-and-removal structure is graded with BW-T03 in the possession and deliverance cluster.

counterpart: Herod struck by an angel and eaten by worms.
invariant: Sudden death with creatures emerging from the body.
mechanic: Instantly kills a non-robotic ground unit; broodlings burst from it.
residual: Acts 12:23 is judgement for accepting worship as a god; Spawn Broodling is a weapon with no moral condition.

counterpart: The snare.
mechanic: Slows units in an area and reveals cloaked ones.
residual: Theme only.

counterpart: 'He is in your hand; only spare his life.' Job is struck with sores from sole to crown.
invariant: The adversary's affliction is bounded: it can push the body down to a floor but cannot cross into death.
mafuba: 001B: a control barrier function. The attack can drive state toward the boundary h(x) = HP - 1 >= 0 but never across it, which is the robust-CBF shape: a safe set the dynamics cannot leave.
mechanic: Units in the area take armour-ignoring damage over time until up to 295 HP is lost or the unit falls to 1-3 HP. Plague cannot kill.
residual: Job's floor is set by God's permission (an outside authority bounds the adversary); Plague's floor is a game rule with no permission-giver. The bound is identical in shape; its source is not.

counterpart: The pillar of cloud between the camps; 'he spread a cloud for a covering'.
invariant: A protective cloud over an army.
mechanic: A cloud under which units take no damage from most ranged attacks; melee, splash, Reaver and Lurker damage still hit.
residual: Role inversion: the protective cloud belongs to the invader. Exodus 14 stops approach entirely; Dark Swarm stops only ranged attacks.

counterpart: Mesha, losing, offers his heir on the wall and the battle turns; the Molech prohibition. Contrast: 'No one takes it from me; I lay it down of my own accord.'
invariant: Power gained by killing one's own in battle, the inverse of self-offering.
mafuba: 001D: a reserve refilled by consuming protected units. 001D must forbid the enforcement path refilling R_reserve from protected state; the reserve may come only from the budget.
mechanic: Kills a friendly Zerg unit to give the Defiler 50 energy, usually mid-battle, to cast Dark Swarm or Plague.
residual: 2 Kings 3:27 does not say where the 'great wrath' came from; the turn of the battle is in the text, the mechanism is not. Consume is routine Zerg economy; Mesha's act is extraordinary and abhorrent. The structure (a commander kills his own for power that turns the fight) holds on four features.

counterpart: The possessed swine rush into the sea and drown.
invariant: Possession ending in the host's destruction.
mechanic: A possessed human produced by an Infested Command Center runs at the enemy and explodes.
residual: The swine's death ends the possession story; Infested Terrans are weapons. Theme only.

residual: As SC2-P06. In Brood War the copies can be made of any target unit, which strengthens the counterfeit reading.

counterpart: Possession (Mark 5), but permanent; closer to a change of allegiance.
invariant: Control transferred at a cost to the controller.
mafuba: 001A: irreversible capture of the actuator fibre (worse than SC2-Z13: nothing to release).
mechanic: Permanently and irreversibly transfers an enemy unit to the caster; the Dark Archon loses all its shields.
residual: Gospel possession is not ownership transfer and is ended by deliverance; Mind Control is permanent. Romans 6:16 (slaves of the one you obey) is closer to allegiance than possession. The cost paid by the caster has no counterpart.

counterpart: They who wait on the LORD renew their strength.
mechanic: All Zerg units and buildings slowly regenerate HP.
residual: Theme only. The Zerg heal because they are living tissue, not by waiting on anyone.

counterpart: The shield of faith that quenches the flaming darts; 'his mercies are new every morning'.
invariant: A renewable outer layer absorbs attacks before the body.
mechanic: A separate layer that takes damage before HP and fully regenerates after about 10 s without damage; EMP strips it; Shield Batteries restore it.
residual: Ephesians 6 assigns the shield to each believer's faith; Protoss shields are hardware. The renewal (Lamentations) is God's mercy; shield regeneration is a timer. Layer-before-body and renewal both match; their sources do not.

counterpart: Balaam's donkey sees the angel standing in the road that Balaam cannot see, until the LORD opens his eyes; Elisha's servant is shown the hidden host. Paul: to another the distinguishing of spirits; the eye cannot say to the hand, 'I have no need of you'.
invariant: Sight is observer-relative. Seeing what is hidden is a specialist faculty that some members have and others lack; the whole body depends on it; and it can be granted.
mechanic: Only specific units and structures can see cloaked and burrowed units; in SC2 they also expose hallucinations. Each army must bring its own detector or it cannot fight hidden enemies at all.
residual: 1 Corinthians 12:10 ('distinguishing between spirits') is about judging true from false, which matches detection's exposure of hallucinations in SC2 but not its exposure of cloaked presence. The 'eyes opened' texts (Numbers 22, 2 Kings 6) carry the presence half. Detection does not expose Changelings (SC2-Z06), so discernment is not reducible to a sensor.
unit: Observer, Overseer, Raven, Science Vessel, Overlord (BW), Missile Turret, Spore Crawler, Photon Cannon; Scanner Sweep

counterpart: If they dig into Sheol, if they climb to heaven, if they hide on Carmel or at the bottom of the sea, I will search them out.
invariant: Every concealment mode is relative to an observer; an observer with full sight defeats all of them.
mechanic: Cloaked or burrowed units cannot be seen or targeted except by detection.
residual: Amos lists hiding modes (dig down, climb up, the sea floor) that read like burrow and air. But the texts say hiding from God never works, while the game makes hiding work against most units. Strong as a contrast; PARTIAL as a mapping.

counterpart: A little leaven leavens the whole lump; the cursed ground; abide in the vine or wither.
invariant: Spreading conditioned ground on which one side's life depends.
mechanic: Creep spreads from sources, speeds Zerg units and is required for most Zerg buildings. It recedes when its source dies, and Zerg buildings left off creep decay.
residual: Leaven does not recede when its source dies; creep does. That dependency fits John 15 (cut off from the source, the branch withers) better than leaven, but the vine is Christ, so the role is inverted for the Zerg. Two texts each fit one half.

counterpart: Apart from me you can do nothing.
invariant: Function depends on staying inside the source's field.
mechanic: Protoss buildings work only inside a Pylon's field. When the Pylon dies they go dark (unpowered), not destroyed, and work again when power returns.
residual: John 15:6 has the branch wither and burn; unpowered Protoss buildings only go dormant. The dependency matches; the consequence does not.

ability: No regeneration; repair-dependent; badly damaged buildings burn
counterpart: Strengthen what remains and is about to die.
mechanic: Terran structures do not heal on their own; badly damaged buildings burn down unless repaired.
residual: Theme only. Read with PASS-01 (Zerg regenerate) and PASS-02 (Protoss renew shields), the three races model three upkeep regimes, but no text pairs them.

counterpart: The prince of the power of the air, the spirit now at work in the sons of disobedience; you cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons.
invariant: Possession through a shared communion channel: whoever is on the channel is reachable.
mafuba: 001A / 001C: a shared bus is an influence path. Isolation must be per node, because a compromise of the shared channel reaches every node attached to it.
mechanic: Amon corrupts the Khala, the Protoss communal psychic link, and takes the Khalai connected to it under his thrall.
residual: The structural point (a shared medium is an influence path) is explicit in the game and only implied in Ephesians 2:2. 1 Corinthians 10 forbids double communion; it does not describe takeover through it.

counterpart: If your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out; it is better to enter life maimed.
invariant: Freedom from a corrupted channel by cutting the organ that connects you to it, at real cost.
mafuba: 001A: isolation by severing (fail-closed on the channel). The Nerazim, already cut off, were not reachable by Amon through the Khala, which is the argument for isolation before compromise.
mechanic: Permanent disconnection from the Khala was impossible unless the nerve cords were cut. The Nerazim cut theirs and were banished. Zeratul cut Artanis's cord to free him from Amon, at the cost of his own life.
residual: Most traditions read Matthew 5:29-30 as hyperbole about the seriousness of sin, not as surgery. The cord itself is not sinful; the channel was hijacked. The cost (loss of communion) matches.

counterpart: The man is found 'clothed and in his right mind'; the boy is left like a corpse, then raised.
invariant: Restoration of the person after removal of the possessing power.
mechanic: The charged artifact destroys nearby Zerg and at least partially de-infests Kerrigan, restoring her human form. Narud later says de-infestation was not the device's intended use.
residual: The Keystone is a weapon whose de-infesting effect was a side effect, and canon says 'at least partially'. Gospel deliverance is by word and intended. Heart of the Swarm later has Kerrigan re-infested by her own choice, which has no Gospel counterpart.

counterpart: The dragon gave his power, his throne and great authority to the beast.
invariant: The adversary remakes a captured person as his empowered vessel.
mechanic: The Overmind has Kerrigan captured and transformed into its chosen weapon, the Queen of Blades.
residual: Revelation 13 describes delegated authority, not a captured human remade. The Overmind's secret purpose (to undermine Amon) has no counterpart.

counterpart: The beast whose mortal wound was healed.
invariant: The adversary imitates resurrection; only a specific power ends it.
mechanic: While the Overmind lived it could reincarnate a slain cerebrate; killing one with Dark Templar void energy prevented reincarnation.
residual: Imitated resurrection is the shared idea. Revelation has no specific power that prevents the return.

counterpart: As BW-Z07: power from consuming one's own; contrast with self-offering.
invariant: Power gained by consuming one's own, the inverse of self-offering.
mechanic: The Ascendant drains life from an ally to restore its own energy; the Power Overwhelming upgrade adds permanent power per Sacrifice.
residual: As BW-Z07. The Tal'darim are a Protoss faction that served Amon, so the consuming pattern sits with Amon's side across races. The ability is named 'Sacrifice', which is borrowed vocabulary; the grade rests on the mechanic, not the name.

counterpart: Babel: one people with one language, and nothing they propose will be impossible; the LORD confuses their speech and scatters them.
invariant: A collective that acts as one through shared communication is broken by disrupting the communication itself.
mafuba: 001C: cutting the coordination channel of a distributed adversary.
mechanic: A Terran device that hampers Zerg psychic communication (in WoL it damages and slows Zerg near it).
residual: The Babel collective is human and voluntary; the Zerg collective is enslaved. At Babel God disrupts, while here the human third faction does. The mechanism (break the shared language) matches.
unit: Psi disrupter (Brood War UED; WoL research)

counterpart: None. Humans possessing the possessors has no text.
invariant: Turning the possessor's method back on him.
mechanic: A Terran structure that mind-controls Zerg creatures.
residual: No honest counterpart. Acts 8:18-20 (Simon trying to buy the power) was considered and rejected: the emulator works.

counterpart: The leech's daughters: 'Give, give'.
mechanic: Dehaka devours other creatures' essence to evolve.
residual: Theme only. A structural cousin of SC-POE-KIT-001 (Kitava as insatiable hunger), not a theological mapping.

counterpart: Restored strength.
mechanic: Heals self and nearby Zerg.
residual: Theme only.

counterpart: As BW-P05.
mechanic: As BW-P05.
residual: As BW-P05.

counterpart: The fallen day star; Satan falling like lightning.
invariant: A member of the creator order who falls and turns against creation.
mechanic: Canon names Amon 'the Dark Voice' and 'the Fallen One'; the Overmind calls him the Fallen One. He is a xel'naga who turned against the cycle and seeks to end all life.
residual: The title is Blizzard's, so the overlap is authored. Isaiah 14 is addressed to the king of Babylon; reading it as Satan's fall is a later tradition. Faction-level mapping belongs to the triad work (COS-17), not to this ability catalogue.
tradition: Patristic reading of Isa 14:12 (Lucifer) as Satan's fall (Origen, Tertullian); many modern commentators read it as a taunt against the Babylonian king.
